html:
Cidade Velha, first called Ribeira Grande, is a town on the island of Santiago in Cape Verde, founded by the Portuguese in 1462. It was the first European colonial town in the tropics.

Cape Verde's islands were empty when Portuguese sailors found them. Settlers grew cotton and sugar with enslaved Africans brought from the nearby coast of Guinea. Ribeira Grande soon became a hub of the Atlantic slave trade: captives were gathered, sold and shipped on to Brazil and the Caribbean. A new mixed people and the Cape Verdean Creole language grew up here.

Its wealth drew attack. Francis Drake raided it in 1585 and French corsairs sacked it in 1712. The capital moved to Praia in 1770, and the old town decayed. Its ruined cathedral, fort and pillory were made a World Heritage Site in 2009.
sum: Cidade Velha, first called Ribeira Grande, is a town on the island of Santiago in Cape Verde, founded by the Portuguese in 1462. It was the first European colonial town in the tropics.
